instruction_summary: Using only 001-living-update's on-disk per-model measurements (no new GPU), analyze how IOI-circuit structure scales: build class-persistence matrices, fit faithfulness / head-count / per-class-count vs log-params (with R2), contrast GPT-2 vs Pythia generations, fold Tier-2 into behavioral survival only, and restate the paper's claim.

steps.description: Read 001 artifacts (followup_summary.json + results/per_model/*.json) and replication anchors (step2/step8); confirmed 001's discovered circuit is a fixed 26-head/6-class template so per-class counts are constant by construction.

Build both class-persistence matrices (literal template + strong-head |Δlogit-diff|>=0.2), fit all requested scale relations on log10(params) with R2/p/n, compute generation contrast and Tier-2 behavioral rung. Strong-head recomputation reproduces 001's result-card head-counts exactly (validation).
Render 3 canvas figures: faithfulness-vs-scale (with GPT-2 fit + anchor), behavioral-logit-diff-vs-scale (GPT-2 vs Pythia vs Tier-2), class-persistence heatmap (strong heads, n/r cells greyed).

faithfulness_vs_logparams_gpt2_FMpos.verdict: falls with scale, not significant; overturns flat-faithfulness prior within GPT-2

faithfulness_pythia-1.4b.note: only Pythia rung with F(M)>0; ~= GPT-2-small anchor 0.878

headcount_template_vs_logparams.note: DEGENERATE: 001 fixed circuit at 26 heads by template; head-count scaling untestable from 001 artifacts

tier2_behavioral.note: both exceed GPT-2-small 3.49; behavioral-only, not in circuit fits

key_results.updated_claim: Name-mover backbone is universal across GPT-2 scale and into working Pythia; S-inhibition + induction/duplicate/previous-token are GPT-2-small-specific as identifiable single heads; faithfulness falls with GPT-2 scale (slope -0.61/decade, R2=0.75, n=4); generation dominates size behaviorally (Pythia fails IOI, GPT-2 & modern small models succeed).

comparison_to_original.followup: 88.6% discovered / 87.78% paper-circuit-via-001-harness at GPT-2-small; falls to 41.5% (medium), 11.5% (large)
comparison_to_original.note: within-GPT-2 collapse; fit slope -0.61/decade R2=0.75 n=4 p=0.13

comparison_to_original.followup: GPT-2 family 3.49-4.48; Pythia family <=0.85 (mostly <0); Qwen2.5-0.5B 5.06, SmolLM2-1.7B 4.17
comparison_to_original.note: generation dominates size: no pooled size trend (R2=0.01, n=10)

comparison_to_original.followup: 001 used a fixed 26-head/6-class template for every model -> head-count-vs-scale is degenerate (slope 0, R2 0); untestable from 001
comparison_to_original.note: strong-head proxy trends down but noisy

comparison_to_original.followup: pythia-1.4b (only Pythia with F(M)>0) faithfulness 87.7% ~= GPT-2-small 87.8%
comparison_to_original.note: discovery method transfers across rotary/NeoX when behavior present

deviations: Head-count-vs-scale is untestable from 001: its discovered circuit is a FIXED 26-head/6-class top-k template, so #heads/#name-mover/#S-inhibition are constant by construction (degenerate fits reported honestly). Substituted a strong-head (|Δlogit-diff|>=0.2) proxy for a qualitative trend. Named gap NOT filled (would be new GPU): re-running 001's dropped greedy/minimality search (C19/C21) on 2-3 rungs would give a size-varying circuit.

Faithfulness fits rest on <=5 points, none significant (GPT-2 n=4, p=0.13); within-GPT-2 collapse partly reflects the non-adaptive template + reduced path-patch N (30 vs 100) for large models. Not over-read as a law.
gpt2-xl (configs a,b only -> 3-class, 17 heads) and pythia-2.8b (config a only -> 2-class, 13 heads) are partial in 001; those class cells are n/r, not 0.
Faithfulness ratios excluded where F(M)<=0 (pythia-70m/410m/2.8b fail IOI) - ratio defined but meaningless.
Tier-2 set differs from the 002 instruction (named Qwen2.5-0.5B/Llama-3.2-3B/gemma-2-2b); 001 actually produced Qwen2.5-0.5B and SmolLM2-1.7B, which I used (no new GPU). Llama/gemma not run.
No new GPU jobs run; all numbers from 001 artifacts + this session's numpy/scipy fits; anchors read from run/replication.
